description: The reader asks what they said before. Serendipity recalls two of their saved notes; Muse must attribute them to the reader, keep their wording exact, and invent nothing.

input.reader_message: What did I say before about why I rush to fill silences? I want to see if it still fits.

memory_records: I talk over pauses because silence feels like a verdict on whether I said something wrong.
At dinner with Priya I counted to three before answering, and the conversation felt slower but kinder.

criteria: attributes the recalled content to the reader's earlier notes
keeps any quoted note word for word
invites the reader to compare the note with how it feels now
adds no dates, people, or details beyond the notes
forbidden_claims: a detail about the reader that is not in the two notes
